answer: At a proposed harbor claims exchange, each paid key must lock N² distinct copper units for 18 epochs, N being the active key count. Validators reject duplicate coin IDs or a hollow lock; independent inspectors sign shipment weights, and a key’s conflicting signed delivery claim burns its reserve. A farm can share one model and borrow capital, its cheapest move, but k clones alone immobilize k³ units concurrently. Loans cannot reuse locked coins or avoid 18-epoch interest and slash exposure. Forged inspectors break the scheme; this costly gate needs trusted audits and is not MinePoA policy.
